title: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 Rubber Bullet Stunt Draws Internet Backlash in Premiere Weekend
excerpt: Viewers slam the Colors TV reality show's pre-elimination task that had four contestants pelted with rubber bullets, calling it dangerous and unacceptable.
body:
• Four Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 contestants — Gaurav Khanna, Karan Wahi, Shagun Sharma, and Vishal Aditya Singh — faced a rubber bullet stunt during the premiere weekend's pre-elimination round
  • Viewers across social media called the stunt "paagalpan" (madness) and questioned whether the show had crossed the line from entertainment into cruelty
  • The controversy adds to an already fraught season, with contestant Shagun Sharma accusing co-star Gaurav Khanna of bullying during filming in Cape Town

Khatron Ke Khiladi 15, the Rohit Shetty-hosted stunt reality show on Colors TV, has barely premiered and is already contending with a wave of viewer outrage. The show's August 1–2 opening weekend featured a pre-elimination round in which four contestants were subjected to rubber bullet fire — and the internet is not having it.

What Happened

During the pre-elimination stunt that aired across the first two episodes, contestants Gaurav Khanna, Karan Wahi, Shagun Sharma, and Vishal Aditya Singh were tasked with enduring rubber bullet impacts as part of a fear-based challenge. Rubber bullets, while non-lethal, can cause severe bruising, welts, and in some cases serious injuries at close range.

https://x.com/indiaforums/status/2084205848080027752

According to the show's stunt matrix, the rubber bullet round determined which contestants advanced safely and which faced further elimination stunts. Karan and Vishal cleared the round and were declared safe, while Gaurav and Shagun were pushed into a subsequent height-based elimination task.

Internet Reacts

Clips from the episode spread rapidly on social media, with viewers using phrases like "Kya paagalpan hai ye" (What madness is this) to describe the stunt. Comments ranged from calling the task "unacceptable" and "inhumane" to questioning whether the show's producers had obtained adequate safety clearances.

"There's a difference between testing courage and inflicting pain for TRP. This crossed a line."

— Viewer comment trending on social media

The backlash mirrors a broader pattern for the Fear Factor franchise in India. Previous seasons have drawn criticism for stunts involving fire, animal encounters, and other extreme physical challenges. Rithvik Dhanjani, a returning veteran on his third appearance, reportedly suffered burn injuries during a fire stunt at the Cape Town shoot earlier this year.

A Season Already Marked by Controversy

The rubber bullet outrage is the second wave of negative attention for Season 15. Before the premiere, actress Shagun Sharma publicly accused fellow contestant Gaurav Khanna of bullying her during the 40-day shoot in Cape Town, South Africa, telling Hindustan Times she "would not want to meet him again." The allegation added a layer of off-screen tension to a season that was already generating buzz for its star-studded cast.

The 13-contestant lineup includes Rubina Dilaik, Jasmin Bhasin, Avinash Mishra, Avika Gor, comedian Harsh Gujral, internet personality Orhan "Orry" Awatramani, child actress-turned-competitor Ruhanika Dhawan, and actress Farrhana Bhatt. The season format pits returning veterans against first-time competitors under the tagline "Darr Ka Naya Daur" (A New Era of Fear).

The Diaspora Angle

For Indian diaspora audiences who grew up watching Fear Factor and its regional adaptations, the rubber bullet controversy cuts both ways. The show remains one of the most-watched Indian reality formats globally, streaming on JioHotstar alongside its Colors TV broadcast. But as conversations about contestant safety and ethical entertainment standards grow louder — from Hollywood to Bollywood — diaspora viewers are increasingly asking whether fear-based entertainment needs stronger guardrails.

What's Next

The show is scheduled to air every weekend at 9 PM IST. The next set of episodes, themed "Psychological Khatra," is slated for August 8–9 and will feature stunts involving animals and candle wax, according to information released by the production team. Whether the makers address the rubber bullet backlash on air or through official statements remains to be seen.

"Meri maa bol rahi thi mat kar Khatron Ke Khiladi."

— Gaurav Khanna, in a pre-season promo, revealing his mother urged him not to join the show

Produced by Banijay Asia (Endemol Shine India), Khatron Ke Khiladi was filmed entirely in Cape Town between May 21 and June 21, 2026. Its premiere had been postponed from July 25 to August 1 due to a TRP blackout across Indian television.
